OFF dedups at entry (vehicle_class_rows_marked_.insert before any read); ON dedups only once store_cached publishes the descriptor, which is after its load (009650DA load, then 00965119 store, as the binary does). A row reached again while its own LandingShip pre-resolve or load runs is resolved again. Checked against this installation (local/g3w2_cycles.py, a Lua table parser over vehicleclasses.lua and both the realistic and arcade bulletclasses.lua / deviceclasses.lua): the pre-store edges are LandingShip plus the device-bullet links mark_vehicle_class_device_bullets_00960230 follows (KamikazeBulletClass and Gun/DefaultGun devices -> DummyKamikazePlane / DummySubmarine / DummyTarget bullets), 13 (realistic) / 15 (arcade), e.g. LevelBomber 32 -> Kamikaze 156, Submarine 81 -> Submarine 4, DiveBomber 110/649 -> DummyTargetVehicle 790, Cargo 224 -> LandingShip 90. No self-loop, no cycle. The 57 Catapult.LaunchedClass edges run after the store and cannot re-enter. A future data cycle among the pre-store edges would recurse without end under ON: the host bullet projection has no bullet-level dedup, while OFF stops at entry.
